difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 912-916: if f from the positive integers to A is surjective, there is a bijection g from Z onto A where Z is either the positive integers or a finite initial segment. The author proof (918-935) defines g by recursion, always taking the first not-yet-used value of f, then runs a case analysis on the size of A and verifies both that g is surjective, using the surjectivity of f, and that g is injective, using the first-unused choice rule. The recursive construction plus the two verifications make this a real argument and not a definition unpacking.
